### bindCommands

**Function** - [src/command-binding.ts:749](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-binding.ts#L749)

```ts
bindCommands(root: Element | Document, options: { bus: BaseBus; }) => () => void
```

bindCommands - the command binding on plain HTML: every `[data-vc-command]`
under `root` (and `root` itself) dispatches its action on `bus`.

The action is the attribute's value, read at press time. `data-vc-target`
and `data-vc-payload` hold JSON. `data-vc-debounce` or `data-vc-throttle`
(ms) pace it at the sender. A form control sends on `input`, or `change`
for a select, a checkbox and a radio, with its value as the payload. A
button is `aria-disabled` and ignores presses while in flight; `vc-loading`
and `vc-error` style it; a failure is announced. Returns `unbind()`.
Elements added later are bound by calling it on them. The display
bindings are `bindDisplay` (src/page-bindings.ts), so a page that only
dispatches carries none of them.

```ts
<button data-vc-command="cartAdd" data-vc-target='{"id":1}'>Add</button>
<input data-vc-command="searchQuery" data-vc-debounce="300">
<script>
  const { bus } = VaporChamber.connect({ endpoint: '/api/vc' });
  VaporChamber.bindCommands(document.body, { bus });
</script>
```

### bindDisplay

**Function** - [src/page-bindings.ts:77](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/page-bindings.ts#L77)

```ts
bindDisplay(root: Element | Document, options: { bus: BaseBus; }) => () => void
```

bindDisplay - display bindings on plain HTML: every bound element under
`root` (and `root` itself) follows a store of `bus` or its command state.

A path is `<store id>.<field>[.<more>]`, rendered at bind time and on each
write of the field (the store's `$onField`, one subscription per element):
`data-vc-text` sets the text, `data-vc-show` hides the element unless the
value is truthy and not an empty array, `data-vc-each` clones its
`<template>` once per entry, a row's paths reading its item and its
`[data-vc-command]` bound as `bindCommands` binds. `data-vc-pending="action"`
(with `data-vc-target`, `{}` when absent, as a command's) sets `vc-loading`
while that action and target is in flight on the bus, from any caller.
`data-vc-router="loading"` (or `"revalidating"`) sets `vc-loading` while
the router loads (or refreshes a page), as the bus hears it from
`routerFacts(router, bus)`: the bindings import no router.
Each path segment is an own property. A store missing at bind time leaves
the markup and warns in development. Returns `unbind()`.

```ts
<span data-vc-text="cart.count">0</span>
<ul data-vc-each="cart.items"><template><li data-vc-text="name"></li></template></ul>
<span data-vc-pending="cartAdd" data-vc-target='{"id":1}'>saving</span>
<script>
  const useCart = VaporChamber.defineChamberStore('cart', { state, reducers });
  useCart(bus);
  VaporChamber.bindDisplay(document.body, { bus });
</script>
```

### cache

**Function** - [src/plugins-extra.ts:66](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/plugins-extra.ts#L66)

```ts
cache(options?: CacheOptions) => PluginParts & { clear(): void; size(): number; }
```

cache - memoize handler results by (action, target) key.
Use with `query()` for read-only commands. The plugin intercepts the
dispatch/query pipeline and returns the cached result if fresh.

```ts
bus.use(cache({ ttl: 60_000, actions: ['getUser*'] }));
bus.query('getUser', { id: 42 }); // handler runs
bus.query('getUser', { id: 42 }); // cache hit, handler skipped
```

### classifyError

**Function** - [src/http-errors.ts:81](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/http-errors.ts#L81)

```ts
classifyError(error: unknown) => ErrorClassification
```

May a retained response stand in for this failure (`serveStaleOnError`)?
Only when the server gave no answer or failed itself: a 5xx, a timeout, no
response. Not a retry rule - a 408 or a 429 is re-sent but not served stale,
and an abort is the caller's. Anything that is not the client's failure
reads as no response.

### commandKey

**Function** - [src/command-bus.ts:1447](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L1447)

```ts
commandKey(action: string, target: any) => string
```

Stable string key for a (action, target) pair. Handles circular refs safely.
Useful for cache invalidation integration (e.g. TanStack Query).

A target keys by its value: a primitive by its String() (so `1` and `'1'`
share a key, by design - tests/isloading-keys.test.ts), an object by its
JSON with keys sorted (keyTextFor, ./canonical), a Number, String, Boolean
or BigInt object as its value. A target JSON cannot serialize does not
share one fallback string with every other: a BigInt, a NaN or an Infinity
inside it is tagged, and a circular, function or symbol target keys by its
identity (tests/commandkey-collisions.test.ts).

An action name holding `:` can share a key with another action -
('a:b', 'c') and ('a', 'b:c') are both `a:b:c`. Escaping the name on every
call measured 25-30% of a primitive key (v1.30.0), so it is a naming rule
instead, decided once (docs/V8-RULES.md rule 3): warned in development and
folded out of production.

### commandState

**Function** - [src/command-state.ts:307](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-state.ts#L307)

```ts
commandState(bus: BaseBus, options?: CommandStateOptions) => CommandState
```

commandState - what is in flight on `bus`, and what failed, for any
framework or none.

Returns a handle on the bus's one shared state: `pending(action, target?)`,
`anyPending`, `errors`, `lastError`, `clear()`, `subscribe(fn)` and
`dispose()`. Every handle reads the same signals. Throws
`core:invalid:bus` for a bus this library did not make.

```ts
const state = commandState(bus);
const saving = state.pending('cartAdd', { id: 1 });
state.subscribe(() => render(saving.value));
// later
state.dispose();
```

### conditionOfStatus

**Function** - [src/failure.ts:152](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/failure.ts#L152)

```ts
conditionOfStatus(status: number) => Condition
```

The condition a status declares (the status table, docs/contract.md 4), saying only
what RFC 9110 says of it, plus 419 (Laravel's expired CSRF token). Every
reader of a backend's answer maps a status through it, here beside the
failure so the http client reads it without the bus.
401 and 419 are `unauthenticated` (a session or token to renew, then the
same request); 403 is `refused` (final). 409 Conflict and 412 Precondition
Failed are `conflict` (the target's state is not the one the request
assumed), not `already`.

### configureReport

```ts
configureReport(options: { format?: ReportFormat; sinks?: readonly ReportSink[]; level?: ReportLevel; } | null) => void
```

Replace the formatter, the sinks or the level floor; an option left out, or
`null`, takes its default (`formatReport`, `[consoleSink]`, `'warn'`). An app
that adds a sink keeps `consoleSink` in its list.

```ts
configureReport({ sinks: [consoleSink, (r) => telemetry.send(r.code, r.context)] });
configureReport({ level: 'error' }); // warnings dropped, errors reported
```

### configureSignal

**Function** - [src/signal.ts:66](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/signal.ts#L66)

```ts
configureSignal(fn: CreateSignal) => void
```

Configure the signal factory. Called once by `chamber.ts` after its async
Vue probe completes; also available to consumers who want a custom signal
implementation.

Dev note: if any signals were created BEFORE this call resolved a reactive
backing, those signals are plain `{ value }` objects forever - writes to them
will not trigger Vue reactivity, while signals created after this call will.
A one-shot dev warning fires in that case; to guarantee a uniform backing,
`await waitForVueDetection()` before the first `signal()` call.

```ts
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { configureSignal } from 'vapor-chamber';
configureSignal(ref);
```

### configureVue

**Function** - [src/chamber.ts:266](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber.ts#L266)

```ts
configureVue(vue: object) => void
```

configureVue - hand the library Vue's module namespace explicitly.

The reliable channel - recommended for every consumer who wants
deterministic Vapor wiring, bundler or not. It seeds the registry
synchronously (no probe race, wrappers' null path becomes unreachable) and
is the one channel that behaves identically however the page obtains Vapor:
bundler alias, import map, or the `esm-browser` dist. Essential on
no-bundler pages, where it is the only channel that cannot come up empty:
Detection otherwise depends on either a global slot Vue overwrites when the
first app mounts (see {@link VUE_GLOBAL_KEY}) or a bare-specifier
`import('vue')` that cannot resolve in a browser at all - so on a
`<script>`-tag page the two automatic channels can both come up empty while
Vapor is sitting right there, and `createVaporChamberApp()` throws
"Vue 3.6+ with Vapor mode required" on a page that has it.

Call this before creating signals or apps. Safe to call more than once; the
last usable namespace wins. Mirrors `configureSignal()` - an explicit
escape hatch that removes a guess.

IMPORTANT: pass the SAME Vue instance the rest of the page uses. Two
separately-imported Vue dist files are two disconnected reactivity engines
(a `ref()` from one is invisible to a `watchEffect` from the other, with no
error) - see the note in `probeVue` below.

```ts
import * as Vue from 'vue/dist/vue.runtime-with-vapor.esm-browser.js';
import { configureVue } from 'vapor-chamber';
configureVue(Vue);
Vue.createVaporApp(App).mount('#app');
```

### countOption

**Function** - [src/bounds.ts:60](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/bounds.ts#L60)

```ts
countOption(value: unknown, fallback: number, min?: number, max?: number) => number
```

Normalize a caller-supplied count, size, depth, attempt cap or delay.

- NaN, or a value `Number()` reads as NaN (undefined, a non-numeric string,
  an object) -> `fallback`, the documented default. A numeric string is its
  number, and `null` and `false` read 0
- below `min`  -> `min`, which catches negatives and -Infinity together
- above `max`  -> `max`; left at `Infinity`, "no bound" passes through intact
- fractional   -> truncated toward zero

`min` defaults to 0 because a cap of zero is meaningful (store nothing) and
distinct from a missing option. Sites where zero is nonsense - an attempt
count, a line length, a circuit threshold - pass `min: 1` and say why.
Delays pass `max: MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`.

### createAsyncCommandBus

**Function** - [src/command-bus.ts:3722](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L3722)

```ts
createAsyncCommandBus<M extends CommandMap = CommandMap>(options?: AsyncCommandBusOptions) => AsyncCommandBus<M>
```

Create an asynchronous command bus. Handlers return Promises.

```ts
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus();
bus.register('user/fetch', async (cmd) => {
  const user = await fetch(`/api/users/${cmd.target.id}`).then(r => r.json());
  return user;
});
const result = await bus.dispatch('user/fetch', { id: 42 });
if (result.ok) console.log(result.value); // { name: 'Alice', ... }
```

### createAsyncSchemaCommandBus

**Function** - [src/schema.ts:531](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/schema.ts#L531)

```ts
createAsyncSchemaCommandBus<S extends BusSchema>(schema: S, options?: AsyncSchemaCommandBusOptions) => AsyncSchemaCommandBus<InferMap<S>>
```

Creates an AsyncCommandBus typed from a flat runtime schema.
Use this when handlers perform async work (API calls, DB, LLM).

```ts
const bus = createAsyncSchemaCommandBus({
  cartAdd: { description: 'Add item', target: { id: 'number' }, payload: { qty: 'number' } },
});
bus.register('cartAdd', async (cmd) => fetchCart(cmd.target.id, cmd.payload.qty));
const result = await bus.synthesize('add 2 of item 5', { adapter: myAdapter });
```

### createChannel

**Function** - [src/plugins-io.ts:104](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/plugins-io.ts#L104)

```ts
createChannel(options: ChannelOptions) => { dispose(): void; isOpen(): boolean; }
```

createChannel - mirror emitted FACTS to every other same-origin context
over a BroadcastChannel.

WHAT CROSSES THE WIRE IS A FACT, NOT A COMMAND, and that is the whole design.
Re-dispatching each command in the receiving tab replicates INTENT: each tab
re-runs the handler and re-derives the outcome. Three things fall out of
that, measured:

  - A handler that is not deterministic does not mirror. Two tabs running
    the same `cartAdd` minted `A-line-1-936891` and `B-line-1-675288` and
    stayed different forever.
  - A tab seeded differently stays different: A ended at 1, B at 6.
  - A handler that dispatches a nested command applied that derivation
    TWICE per tab, because each tab derived its own and then received the
    peer's. Suppressing the receive side alone did not fix it (6 runs became
    5, not 4): the ORIGINATING tab was still broadcasting its derivations.
    Fixing that by inference needs the core to distinguish a root dispatch
    from a derived one, which it does not, and adding a counter to do so
    would tax every dispatch on the bus.

Emitting the fact removes the question instead of answering it. The app says
what crosses by emitting it; a derivation is not a fact unless the app says
so, so there is nothing to infer and no counter to pay for. The receiving tab
APPLIES the values the sender computed rather than recomputing them, which is
the ordinary CQRS split - a command is intent, an event is something that
already happened - and it is what makes a non-deterministic handler a
non-issue.

IT ALSO LEAVES THE DISPATCH CHAIN. As a plugin this cost more than half the
bus's dispatch throughput, on every dispatch of every action, whether or not
it synced. Measured over 11 shuffled rounds of 200,000 dispatches with
`gc()` per round, against a byte-identical self-control arm: bare bus 1.000,
as a plugin 0.459 (control 0.454), as an `onAfter` listener 0.538, and on the
fast lane 0.867. The correctness fix and the performance fix are the same
change.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT DO. Facts mirror, seeds do not: a tab that starts from
different state stays different unless the facts are absolute ("the count is
2") rather than relative ("add one"). And a payload crosses through the
structured clone algorithm, so it cannot carry functions - see the DEV
warning below.

```ts
const lane = createFastLane()
lane.on('cartAdded', (fact) => applyToCart(fact))   // local AND remote land here

bus.register('cartAdd', (cmd) => {
  const fact = computeAdd(cmd.target)
  applyToCart(fact)
  lane.emit('cartAdded', fact)                      // this is what crosses tabs
})

const tabSync = createChannel({ channel: 'vapor-chamber:app', lane, events: ['cartAdded'] })
tabSync.dispose() // on unmount
```

### createEchoBridge

**Function** - [src/transports.ts:1223](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/transports.ts#L1223)

```ts
createEchoBridge(options: EchoBridgeOptions) => { install(bus: BaseBus): void; dispose(): void; }
```

createEchoBridge - wire Laravel Echo / Reverb realtime channels to the bus.

Protocol-aware over the generic WS transport: subscribes public / private /
presence channels and routes each broadcast to `bus.emit()`, after writing
the store states its payload declares under `stores` (or a command via
`onBroadcast`). Presence membership (`here` / `joining` / `leaving`) is emitted
too. Receive-only by design - outbound commands still go through the HTTP
transport. Pass your own Echo instance; the bridge never imports laravel-echo, so
non-Laravel consumers don't pay for it.

```ts
import Echo from 'laravel-echo';
const echo = new Echo({ broadcaster: 'reverb', ... });
const realtime = createEchoBridge({
  echo,
  channels: [
    { name: 'orders', type: 'private', events: ['OrderShipped', 'OrderCancelled'] },
    { name: 'lobby',  type: 'presence', events: ['MessagePosted'] },
  ],
});
realtime.install(bus);   // OrderShipped -> bus.emit('OrderShipped', payload)
// on teardown:
realtime.dispose();
```

### createSseBridge

**Function** - [src/transports.ts:1107](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/transports.ts#L1107)

```ts

```

createSseBridge - server-sent events bridge for unidirectional server push.

SSE is receive-only: the server pushes events to the client. Without
`onEvent`, each event is a push: its `data` read as JSON, each store state
under `stores` written by that store, then the event emitted on the bus by
its type, never dispatched (docs/contract.md 4). Data that is not JSON,
such as the `</stream>` that ends Laravel's event stream, is ignored.

```ts
const sse = createSseBridge({ url: '/api/vc/stream', events: ['update'] })
// event: update, data: {"stores":{"cart":{...}}} -> the cart store's state
sse.install(bus)

// Later, on component unmount:
sse.dispose()
```

createTransitionBridge - wire Vue transition hooks to bus commands.

Framework-agnostic: accepts any BaseBus (sync or async). Use this in
non-Vue contexts or when you need explicit lifecycle control.

```ts
const bus = createCommandBus();

  cmd.target.animate([{ opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1 }], { duration: 300 });
});

// Pass t.onEnter, t.onLeave, etc. to <Transition> or call them manually

On a vDOM app, `<Transition mode="out-in">` with this bridge needs an ASYNC
bus. On a sync bus the bridge calls `done()` at once, so the leave finishes
synchronously, and Vue's vDOM `out-in` then throws and renders nothing
(tests/transition-done-timing-fixture.test.ts). That is Vue's defect,
reported as vuejs/core#15727, a fix proposed in vuejs/core#11824. Vapor's
`<Transition>` and the default mode are not affected (same test).
```

### defineSchema

**Function** - [src/schema.ts:154](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/schema.ts#L154)

```ts
defineSchema<const S extends BusSchema>(schema: S) => S
```

defineSchema - identity helper that PRESERVES field-type literals, so the
schema keeps its inference power. Without it, `{ id: 'number' }` widens to
`Record<string, string>` and every inferred type collapses to `any`.

The complete one-source-of-truth wiring:

```ts
// commands.ts - define once
export const schema = defineSchema({
  cartAdd: {
    description: 'Add a product to the cart',
    target:  { id: 'number', name: 'string' },
    payload: { qty: 'number' },
    result:  { count: 'number', total: 'number' },
  },
  cartCheckout: {
    description: 'Charge the cart and place the order',
    authorize: 'checkout',           // -> Gate::forUser($user)->authorize('checkout', ...)
    target:  { cartId: 'number' },
  },
});

// -> typed schema bus (validation + LLM tools included)
const bus = createSchemaCommandBus(schema);

// -> typed SHARED bus for every useCommand()/getCommandBus() call site
declare module 'vapor-chamber' {
  interface GlobalCommands extends InferMap<typeof schema> {}
}
setCommandBus(bus);

// -> Laravel stubs + registry: node scripts/generate-laravel.mjs commands.mjs
// -> agent tools: bus.toTools() / vapor-chamber/mcp
```

An app's own transport: `send` answers the command, and `local()` runs the
action's local handler (or the missing-handler outcome), its fallback. A
throw or a rejection fails the dispatch as `transport:failed:send`. A send
that calls `local()` declares `localFallback: true`: only then may its
actions have a handler, `optimistic` aside
(tests/register-shadow-check.test.ts).

```ts
const offlineFirst = defineTransport((cmd, local) => (navigator.onLine ? send(cmd) : local()), { localFallback: true })
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus({ transport: offlineFirst })
```

defineVaporCommand - a command for hot paths in Vapor mode: one action, its
handler registered with the composable, and a dispatch that writes no state.

Ideal for high-frequency, fire-and-forget patterns where no busy or error
state is shown: scroll-position tracking, mousemove
sampling, telemetry / metrics events, debounced search, autosave.
`{ debounce: ms }` or `{ throttle: ms }` paces the dispatch at the sender
(`pace`): a paced dispatch returns a promise.

One handler per action, the newest registration still live: two pages
that define one action each answer while on screen, the older one again
once the newer unmounts, and a page cached by KeepAlive releases its
handler until it returns. tests/register-live-owner-fixture.test.ts.

```ts
const { dispatch } = defineVaporCommand('telemetryEvent', (cmd) => {
  // forward to whatever metrics / analytics SDK you use
  sendMetric(cmd.target.name, cmd.target.params);
});
dispatch({ name: 'page_view', params: { page: '/landing' } });
```

defineVaporComponent - define a Vapor component with proper type inference.

Wraps Vue's `defineVaporComponent()`. Use this to get full

```ts
  props: { count: Number },

    return div;
```

### defineVaporCustomElement

**Function** - [src/chamber-vapor.ts:145](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber-vapor.ts#L145)

```ts
defineVaporCustomElement<T = any>(options: object, extraOptions?: object) => T | null
```

defineVaporCustomElement - create a custom element backed by Vapor rendering.

Wraps Vue's `defineVaporCustomElement()`. The generated custom
element uses Vapor's compiler-optimized rendering instead of the VDOM, giving
zero-overhead DOM updates inside shadow DOM. Safe to call with a reused
options object, and children re-render on reactive prop changes (Vue 3.6.0-beta.14+).

Returns null if the Vapor runtime (Vue 3.6+) is not detected - check before calling
`customElements.define()`.

```ts
import { defineVaporCustomElement } from 'vapor-chamber';
const MyEl = defineVaporCustomElement({
  props: { label: String },
  // A Vapor setup() returns a BLOCK - real DOM nodes - not a render
  // function or h() output. An SFC's compiler builds this from its template.
  setup(props) {
    const span = document.createElement('span');
    span.textContent = String(props.label);
    return span;
  }
});
if (MyEl) customElements.define('vc-greeting', MyEl);
```

### defineWidget

**Function** - [src/widget.ts:104](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/widget.ts#L104)

```ts
defineWidget(tagName: string, component: WidgetComponent, options?: WidgetOptions) => boolean
```

defineWidget - register a Vapor custom element by tag, in one line.

`when` picks the moment (default `load`): `load` defines it now; `visible`
when the first element of that tag on the page enters the viewport (one
IntersectionObserver for every widget; with none on the page, now);
`idle` in `requestIdleCallback` (a 1 ms timer where it is missing). A
component given as a loader is imported at that moment. The other options
go to `defineVaporCustomElement`. Returns `false`, and defines nothing,
when there is no `customElements` registry or Vue 3.6 Vapor is not
detected; `true` once the tag is defined or
will be.

## Naming convention - use the `vc-` prefix

`<vc-cart/>` reads as a vapor-chamber widget in Blade or Twig, avoids
clashing with a host page's elements, and `grep -r "<vc-"` finds every one.
The HTML spec needs a hyphen in a custom element's name; `vc-` gives it. A
project with its own brand prefix (`<acme-cart/>`) keeps it.

## What `setup()` returns

A Vapor component returns a BLOCK - real DOM nodes - not a vnode. On a page
with no build step there is no compiler to turn a template into one, so
build the nodes directly: `h()` is not on the `VaporChamber` global in any
variant, and it produces a vnode, the vDOM shape Vapor replaced. Pinned by
`tests/vapor/widget-shape.test.ts`, which mounts a real widget.

## A function set on a property

`el.onSave = fn` hands `setup(props)` the function itself, from Vue
3.6.0-rc.10. Pinned by the same file.

```ts
<script src=".../vapor-chamber-elements.iife.min.js"></script>
<script type="module">
  // Vue ships Vapor as esm-browser only, so a classic page loads it as a
  // module and hands it over; without it defineWidget returns false.
  const Vue = await import('https://.../vue.runtime-with-vapor.esm-browser.prod.js');
  VaporChamber.configureVue(Vue);
  VaporChamber.defineWidget('vc-cart', {
    props: { sku: String },
    setup(props) {
      const span = document.createElement('span');
      span.textContent = `SKU ${props.sku}`;
      return span;
    }
  }, { when: 'visible' });
</script>
<vc-cart sku="ABC-123"></vc-cart>
```

### emitDOMEvent

**Function** - [src/widget.ts:175](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/widget.ts#L175)

```ts
emitDOMEvent(el: Element, eventName: string, detail?: any, options?: { bubbles?: boolean; composed?: boolean; cancelable?: boolean; }) => boolean
```

Emit a real DOM `CustomEvent` from inside a widget so host pages can
subscribe with `addEventListener`.

A custom element's own `emit(...)` reaches its host as a `CustomEvent`
that neither bubbles nor crosses a shadow root (rc.11, VueElementBase), so
a listener on the host hears it while `document`, `window` and the
containers around it do not. An `emit` from a component nested inside the
widget stays in Vue's event system. For widgets that need to reach the
surrounding page, this dispatches a bubbling, composed `CustomEvent`.

Pattern adapted from
[vue-custom-element](https://github.com/karol-f/vue-custom-element)'s
`customEmit` helper (Karol-F, MIT), which predates Vue 3.6's Vapor.

| parameter | description |
|---|---|
| `el` | - the custom element instance (host element) |
| `eventName` | - DOM event name (kebab-case is conventional for custom events) |
| `detail` | - payload attached to event.detail |
| `options` | - bubbles/composed/cancelable. Defaults: bubbles=true, composed=true   (composed=true escapes shadow-DOM boundaries by default - required   for events to reach light-DOM listeners on the host page). |

**Returns:** `false` if `event.preventDefault()` was called by a listener, `true` otherwise.

```ts
Widget side
button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
const host = e.target.getRootNode().host;   // escape the shadow root
VaporChamber.emitDOMEvent(host, 'cart-added', { sku: 'X' });
});
```

```ts
Host page
document.querySelector('vc-cart').addEventListener('cart-added', (e) => {
console.log(e.detail.sku);   // 'X'
});
```

### failureCondition

**Function** - [src/command-bus.ts:51](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L51)

```ts
failureCondition(error: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal) => Condition
```

Any failure's condition, read by contract (docs/contract.md 4, reading by contract): a library
failure's own code; an HTTP status (another client's `response.status`) through the
status table; a timeout by its name; a cancel, named `AbortError` or the
`signal`'s own reason (`_isCancel`); the Fetch standard's `TypeError` for no
response at all, `lost`. Anything else - a handler's own throw, a test
diagnostic - is `failed` (docs/contract.md rule 8). Pass the command's
`signal` to read an abort with the caller's own Error as `aborted`
(tests/abort-custom-reason.test.ts).


history - undo/redo of the commands dispatched on `bus`, recorded from the
call on. Not a plugin: the recorder is the ledger's (ledger.ts), so it
records what the caller got wherever plugins sit. undo() dispatches
`<action>$undo`, which runs the inverse registered with `{ undo: fn }` via
bus.register(); with none it only moves the step. `undoAction` /

### httpTransport

**Function** - [src/transports.ts:530](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/transports.ts#L530)

```ts
httpTransport(options: HttpTransportOptions) => Transport
```

httpTransport - commands sent over fetch, as JSON.

The backend receives `{ command, target, payload, meta? }`, with
`Accept: application/json, application/problem+json` and a keyed command's
`Idempotency-Key`, and answers
`{ state, stores? }`, `{ stores }` or `{ redirect }` on success, and a
non-2xx RFC 9457 problem on failure,
read as `remote:<condition of its status>:<code>` (docs/contract.md 4).

Features: multi-source CSRF token reading (meta tag / cookie / hidden input),
automatic CSRF-expiry refresh on HTTP 419 (Laravel Sanctum convention by
default, configurable for other frameworks), session-expiry detection on
401, request timeout, per-call AbortSignal. It sends each command once: the
async bus re-sends through it by the failure's condition, after a declared
Retry-After (docs/retry.md). After a 429 or 503 that declares a wait, it
sends no command for that action until the wait ends: each fails at once as
`transport:limited:held`, which the bus waits out (docs/retry.md, The hold).

With `batch`, every command sent within the window goes as ONE POST:

  { commands: [{ id, command, target, payload, meta?, headers? }, ...] }

a keyed command's `Idempotency-Key` in its `headers`, matched back against:

  { results: [{ id, status, headers, state, stores? }, { id, status, headers, redirect }, { id, status, headers, problem }, ...] }

Each result carries the command's own `status` and `headers` (OData JSON
batch): a problem with no status reads the result's, and its
`Retry-After` sets the wait as a single response's does. Each dispatch
settles on its own result: the coalescing is invisible to the call site.

```ts
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus({
  transport: httpTransport({ endpoint: '/api/vc', csrf: true }),
  retry: { actionPolicies: { 'cart*': 'idempotent' } },
})
await bus.dispatch('cartAdd', product, { quantity: 2 })
```

### idempotent

**Function** - [src/plugins-extra.ts:559](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/plugins-extra.ts#L559)

```ts
idempotent(options?: IdempotentOptions) => PluginParts
```

idempotent - make duplicate dispatches a no-op against the handler/backend.

The client-side half of exactly-once delivery: it collapses repeats of the
same logical command - double-clicked Checkout, an auto-retry, a reconnect
that replays a queued action - so the handler (and the backend it calls) runs
**once**. Concurrent duplicates share the first in-flight promise; sequential
duplicates within `ttl` get the cached result. Failures are NOT cached, so a
genuine retry after an error still runs.

Pairs with `register({ exclusive })` (orders same-key commands locally) and the HTTP
transport, which forwards the stamped `cmd.meta.idempotencyKey` as an
`Idempotency-Key` header so the backend runs a re-sent request once - the
wire half of exactly-once. That key is the dispatch's id, or the `key`
option's value: the content key stays in the browser. The transport is the
work, inside every plugin, so the key is stamped before the request is built.

```ts
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus({ transport: httpTransport({ endpoint: '/commands', csrf: true }) });
bus.use(idempotent({ actions: ['order*'] }));
// two rapid orderCreate dispatches -> one handler run, one backend write
```

indexedDbStorage - an IndexedDB storage for a store's `persist`. Prefer it

| parameter | description |
|---|---|

```ts

```

### onSettled

**Function** - [src/settled.ts:61](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/settled.ts#L61)

```ts
onSettled<R extends MaybeAsyncResult>(result: R, fn: (settled: CommandResult) => CommandResult) => R
```

Run `fn` once the result is real, and PRESERVE SYNC-NESS: a sync result
stays sync, so the sync bus never waits a microtask for it. Only a promise
takes the async arm.

THERE IS NO REJECTION ARM. One call site in `chamber.ts` (runDispatch)
hand-rolls the check instead: a dispatch promise that REJECTS never reaches
`fn`, and it has cleanup that must run anyway (clearing a loading flag,
recording the error), so it spells out
`.then(onOk, onErr)` plus the success body again for the sync path. Through
`onSettled` with a rejection arm, the sync path would build its two
callbacks on every dispatch, since they capture that dispatch's state: a
closure per call on a hot path (docs/V8-RULES.md rule 4). The duplicated
bodies stay until an `npm run ab` says the closures cost nothing.

### pace

**Function** - [src/pace.ts:100](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/pace.ts#L100)

```ts
pace(send: Send, options: PaceOptions) => Paced
```

pace - a dispatch paced at the sender, keyed by action and target
(`commandKey`, objects by value).

- `debounce: ms` runs the latest call per key once `ms` pass with no newer
  one, and answers it with the real result. An earlier call of the burst
  answers `pace:aborted:dispatch` and never reaches the bus. Pass what
  changes on each call (the typed text) as the PAYLOAD: in the target, each
  value is its own key and nothing coalesces.
- `throttle: ms` runs the first call per key at once and answers a repeat
  inside `ms` with `pace:limited:dispatch` (`context.retryIn`, `wait`).

Latest wins in both: a run of a key aborts that key's run still in flight
(`dispatch(..., { signal })`), so a stale answer settles aborted and never
lands after a newer one. `dispose()` aborts what is in flight.

A `$` action (a reset, an undo) runs at once, unpaced. A paced call always
returns a promise, on either bus. NaN is no wait, one past the timer's
maximum the maximum. tests/pace.test.ts.

```ts
const search = pace(bus.dispatch, { debounce: 300 });
input.addEventListener('input', async () => {
  const r = await search('searchQuery', {}, input.value);
  if (r.ok) render(r.value);
});
```

whatever wrote it. An async storage is read when it answers; the writes made

reducer runs again, a state set whatever came before is kept), and nothing is

### setCommandBus

**Function** - [src/shared-bus.ts:55](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/shared-bus.ts#L55)

```ts
setCommandBus(bus: CommandBus | AsyncCommandBus) => void
```

Replace the shared bus instance.

SSR WARNING: the shared bus is a module global - one per Node process, not
per request. The set-render-reset pattern (see ssr.ts) is only safe when
requests render strictly one at a time. Under CONCURRENT SSR renders,
interleaved requests stomp each other's bus: handlers and state leak across
requests. For concurrent servers, don't use the shared bus on the server -
create a bus per request and pass it explicitly (every composable and plugin
accepts a `bus` option / argument).

Accepts either bus flavor - the composables' dispatch path already handles
thenable results (`runDispatch` awaits them), so an AsyncCommandBus works at
runtime. `getCommandBus()`'s static type is `CommandBus`.

Call it before anything calls `getCommandBus()`. Replacing the bus
`getCommandBus()` already created and handed out splits the app: code that
holds the old bus keeps dispatching to it. In DEV that replacement warns,
once (tests/shared-bus-fallback-warning.test.ts); setting the same bus again,
as the HMR shim does, or setting after `resetCommandBus()`, does not.

opens asks for the state and takes the lead's answer. Outside a page or a
worker (a server), without `BroadcastChannel` or without Web Locks, nothing


### supersede

**Function** - [src/plugins-extra.ts:742](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/plugins-extra.ts#L742)

```ts
supersede(options?: SupersedeOptions) => PluginParts
```

supersede - auto-cancel the previous in-flight dispatch for the same key.

Built for rapid-fire reads that can overwrite each other in flight - a
search box re-querying on every keystroke, a filter changing before the
previous fetch lands. Without it, a slow first response can arrive AFTER a
faster second one and clobber it with stale data. With it, the first
dispatch's AbortSignal fires the instant a second dispatch for the same key
starts - `httpTransport` forwards `cmd.signal` to `fetch()`, so the
stale request is genuinely cancelled, not merely ignored once it resolves.
With `batch`, it settles the stale command at once, drops it
from a batch not yet sent, and cancels a sent batch once every command in
it has aborted (tests/batching-abort.test.ts). A handler that passes `cmd.signal` to
`createHttpClient().get()` is cancelled the same way, even when its GET
joined one already in flight (see the client's `dedupe`).

**Async bus only**: its `begin` step hands the bus the signal the work
runs under, which only a cancelable async dispatch carries.

```ts
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus({ transport: httpTransport({ endpoint: '/api/vc' }) });
bus.use(supersede({ actions: ['productSearch'] }));
// three quick productSearch dispatches -> only the last one's response is
// ever awaited; the first two are aborted mid-flight, not just discarded
```

synthesize - natural language -> bus dispatch via LLM tool use.

Requires an `adapter` - a function that takes tool definitions + user text
and returns a ToolCallInput. This keeps vapor-chamber vendor-agnostic:
bring your own Anthropic SDK, OpenAI SDK, or custom proxy.

```ts
const result = await synthesize(schema, bus, 'add 2 of item 5', {
  adapter: async (tools, text) => {
    const res = await anthropic.messages.create({ tools, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: text }] });
    const toolUse = res.content.find(b => b.type === 'tool_use');
    return { name: toolUse.name, input: toolUse.input };
  },
});
```

untracked - run `fn` without its reactive reads becoming dependencies of

A dispatch is an ACTION, not a read: nothing it touches should make the
caller re-run. Every composable in this module already applies this to its
own dispatches, so you only need it when calling a **raw bus** from inside a
reactive effect:

```ts
import { untracked, getCommandBus } from 'vapor-chamber';
watchEffect(() => {
  // without untracked(), anything the HANDLER reads becomes a dependency
  // of this effect, and it re-runs on state it never mentions
  untracked(() => getCommandBus().dispatch('cartSync', cart));
});

No-op when Vue is not present, so it is safe to leave in shared code.
Vue fixed the same class of bug twice in 3.6.0-rc.3 (#15203, #15204) by
suspending tracking around callbacks - this is that idea at the bus edge.
```

```ts
useCommand<B extends BaseBus = CommandBus<CommandMap>, D extends number | undefined = undefined, T extends number | undefined = undefined>(options?: BusOption<B> & PaceOption<D, T>) => { dispatch: <A extends keyof SharedCommandMap & string>(action: A, target: TargetOf<SharedCommandMap, A>, payload?: PayloadOf<SharedCommandMap, A>) => PacedOn<B, CommandResult<ResultOf<SharedCommandMap, A>>, D, T>; pending: <A extends keyof SharedCommandMap & string>(action: A, target?: TargetOf<SharedCommandMap, A>) => Readonly<Signal<boolean>>; register: <A extends keyof SharedCommandMap & string>(action: A, handler: (cmd: Command<A, TargetOf<SharedCommandMap, A>, PayloadOf<SharedCommandMap, A>>) => ResultOf<SharedCommandMap, A> | Promise<ResultOf<SharedCommandMap, A>>, opts?: RegisterOptions) => () => void; on: (pattern: string, listener: (cmd: Command, result: CommandResult) => void) => () => void; emit: (event: string, data?: any) => void; dispose: () => void; }
```

useCommand - command dispatch with bus subscriptions, cleaned up with the scope.

`{ debounce: ms }` or `{ throttle: ms }` paces its `dispatch` at the sender
(`pace`): a paced dispatch returns a promise, and search as you type passes
the typed text as the payload so the keystrokes share one key.

Returns `dispatch`, `pending(action, target?)` (the bus's command state for
that key, `commandState`), plus `register` / `on` / `emit` for handlers and
listeners, all released on scope disposal (`onScopeDispose`). Vapor-safe -
works in `<script setup vapor>` and VDOM alike, with no
`getCurrentInstance()` dependency. A dispatch's own failure is its result.
The bus's recent failures are `useSharedCommandState().errors`.

```ts
const { dispatch, register, pending } = useCommand();
register('cartAdd', (cmd) => addToCart(cmd.target));
const adding = pending('cartAdd', { id: product.id });
dispatch('cartAdd', { id: product.id });
```

### useCommandError

```ts
useCommandError(options?: ScopeOptions & { maxSize?: number; } & BusOption) => { errors: Signal<{ cmd: Command; error: Error; timestamp: number; }[]>; latestError: Signal<Error | null>; clearErrors: () => void; dispose: () => void; }
```

useCommandError - component-scoped error boundary for command failures.

Subscribes to the bus and captures all failed command results reactively.
Optional `actions` and `actionFilter` narrow which actions are tracked.

```ts
const { latestError, errors, clearErrors } = useCommandError()

// Only watch cart commands
const { latestError } = useCommandError({ actions: ['cart*'] })
```

### useCommandGroup

**Function** - [src/chamber.ts:1178](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber.ts#L1178)

```ts
useCommandGroup<B extends BaseBus = CommandBus<CommandMap>>(namespace: string, options?: BusOption<B>) => { dispatch: (action: string, target: any, payload?: any) => ResultOn<B>; query: (action: string, target: any, payload?: any) => ResultOn<B>; emit: (event: string, data?: any) => void; register: (action: string, handler: Handler, opts?: RegisterOptions) => () => void; use: (plugin: PluginParts) => () => void; on: (pattern: string, listener: Listener) => () => void; namespace: string; dispose: () => void; }
```

useCommandGroup - namespace isolation for large apps and multi-team projects.

All dispatch/register/on calls are automatically prefixed with the namespace
in camelCase. This prevents action name collisions when composing multiple
feature modules.

```ts
// Cart feature
const cart = useCommandGroup('cart')
cart.register('add', handler)    // registers 'cartAdd'
cart.dispatch('add', product)    // dispatches 'cartAdd'
cart.on('*', listener)           // listens to 'cart*'

// Orders feature - completely isolated
const orders = useCommandGroup('orders')
orders.dispatch('cancel', { id }) // dispatches 'ordersCancel'
```

### useCommandQuery

**Function** - [src/chamber.ts:1138](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber.ts#L1138)

```ts
useCommandQuery<B extends BaseBus = CommandBus<CommandMap>>(options?: BusOption<B>) => { query: (action: string, target: any, payload?: any) => ResultOn<B>; data: Signal<any>; loading: Signal<boolean>; }
```

useCommandQuery - CQRS read-side composable with reactive state.

Wraps bus.query() with reactive `data` and `loading` signals. A query's own
failure is its result. The bus's recent failures are
`useSharedCommandState().errors`.
query() runs the rules, the steps, the handler and the afterHooks; its
start is not counted as pending.

Supports both sync and async buses - if the result is a Promise, loading
stays true until it resolves.

```ts
const { query, data, loading } = useCommandQuery();
const result = query('getUser', { id: 42 });
// data.value = result.value after query completes
```

### useSharedCommandState

**Function** - [src/chamber.ts:1040](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber.ts#L1040)

```ts
useSharedCommandState<B extends BaseBus = CommandBus<CommandMap>>(options?: UseSharedCommandStateOptions<B>) => CommandState
```

useSharedCommandState - the bus's command state (`commandState`) as a Vue
view: the same handle, released when the component's scope ends.

Every caller on one bus reads the same signals, so 50 components cost one
state, not 100 signals. `pending(action, target?)` is in flight for that
key, `anyPending` for any command, bus-wide: a dispatch from anywhere counts.

```ts
const { pending, anyPending, lastError } = useSharedCommandState();
const saving = pending('cartAdd', { id: product.id });
<Button :disabled="anyPending">Save</Button>
```

### useVaporAsyncCommand

**Function** - [src/chamber-vapor.ts:318](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber-vapor.ts#L318)

```ts
useVaporAsyncCommand(asyncBus?: { dispatch: (action: string, target: any, payload?: any) => Promise<CommandResult>; }) => { dispatch: (action: string, target: any, payload?: any) => Promise<CommandResult>; pending: (action: string, target?: unknown) => Readonly<Signal<boolean>>; dispose: () => void; }
```

useVaporAsyncCommand - async-aware command dispatch for Vapor components
used inside Suspense boundaries.

Vue 3.6.0-beta.10+ hydrates async components under VDOM Suspense. This
composable wraps an AsyncCommandBus dispatch, untracked, and
gives `pending(action, target?)` (the bus's command state for that key,
`commandState`), making it safe for `<script setup vapor>` components that
await async operations. Error-boundary rendering and scheduler-flush
behavior around async components are Vue runtime concerns (per-beta detail:
whitepaper appendix B, and log section 37).

The dispatch function returns a Promise<CommandResult>, matching the
AsyncCommandBus interface. Use this when your commands hit async transports
(httpTransport, wsTransport) and you need awaitable results. A dispatch's
own failure is its result.

Vue 3.6.0-rc.8: an awaiting `<script setup vapor>` compiles to an
`async setup()` that uses runtime-core's `withAsyncContext` and returns its
template as a render closure, and it registers with the NEAREST `<Suspense>`.
Composables called after the `await` - this one, `useCommand()` - arm their
cleanup on the restored component scope, including when the app unmounts
during the await. Pinned by tests/async-vapor-setup-fixture.test.ts.

```ts
// In a <script setup vapor> component under <Suspense>:
import { useVaporAsyncCommand } from 'vapor-chamber';
const { dispatch, pending } = useVaporAsyncCommand(asyncBus);
const creating = pending('orderCreate');
const result = await dispatch('orderCreate', { items: cart });
```

### wsTransport

**Function** - [src/transports.ts:795](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/transports.ts#L795)

```ts
wsTransport(options: WsTransportOptions) => Transport & { connect(): void; disconnect(): void; isConnected(): boolean; connected: Signal<boolean>; outbox: Outbox; }
```

wsTransport - commands over one WebSocket, with reconnect and an outbox.

Commands are sent as JSON frames over a persistent WebSocket connection.
While the socket is not open, a command is held in the transport's own
outbox (`outbox`, in memory: at most 100, each for at most `timeout`) and
answers an `Accepted` whose `done` settles with the reply once sent. An
app outbox (`createAsyncCommandBus({ outbox })`) that covers the action
holds it instead, durably when it has storage. `disconnect()`, and a close
with no reconnect left, settle the transport's own held callers.
A frame with no `id`, `{ event, data }`, is the server's push: the store
states under `data.stores` written, then the event emitted on the bus that
declares this transport, never dispatched (docs/contract.md 4).

```ts
const ws = wsTransport({ url: 'wss://api.example.com/vc' })
const bus = createAsyncCommandBus({ transport: ws })
ws.connect()
```

### BusError

**Class** - [src/failure.ts:66](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/failure.ts#L66)

```ts
BusError: typeof BusError
```

BusError - a failure the library, a plugin or a transport raised.

Extends native Error so it works everywhere errors work (catch, result.error).
`code` is `owner:condition:subject`; `ownerOf()` and `conditionOf()` read its
parts. Severity is not on it: whoever logs a failure decides how loud it is
(the catalogue's `severity` is the suggested level).

```ts
const result = bus.dispatch('missing', {});
if (!result.ok && result.error instanceof BusError) {
  console.log(result.error.code);           // 'core:missing:handler'
  console.log(conditionOf(result.error));   // 'missing'
  console.log(result.error.action);         // 'missing'
}
```

## Interfaces

### AsyncCommandBus

**Interface** - [src/command-bus.ts:696](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L696)

```ts
export interface AsyncCommandBus<M extends CommandMap = CommandMap> extends BaseBus {
  /**
   * Async dispatch with optional `AbortSignal`. If `options.signal` is already
   * aborted at call time, resolves immediately with `core:aborted:dispatch`
   * without invoking the handler. If aborted mid-flight, the handler observes
   * `cmd.signal.aborted === true`; the HTTP transport propagates the signal
   * to the underlying fetch automatically. A handler or plugin that rethrows
   * the signal's reason gets the same `core:aborted:dispatch`. Every abort the
   * bus builds is a BusError named `AbortError`, with the reason as `cause`. A
   * custom Error reason (`ac.abort(myError)`) is never wrapped, at call time or
   * mid-flight: it passes through as itself.
   */
  dispatch<A extends keyof M & string>(
    action: A,
    target: TargetOf<M, A>,
    payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>,
    options?: DispatchOptions,
  ): Promise<CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>>;
  /** Read-only dispatch - runs the rules, the steps and the handler, fires afterHooks. */
  query<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, target: TargetOf<M, A>, payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>): Promise<CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>>;
  /** Fire a domain event - notifies on() listeners, no handler required, no result. */
  emit(event: string, data?: any): void;
  dispatchBatch(commands: BatchCommand[], options?: BatchOptions): Promise<BatchResult>;
  /** `null`: the options of an action a transport sends, with no handler (`_checkHandler`). */
  register<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, handler: ((cmd: Command<A, TargetOf<M, A>, PayloadOf<M, A>>) => ResultOf<M, A> | Promise<ResultOf<M, A>>) | null, options?: RegisterOptions): () => void;
  /** Installs a plugin: the bus places each of its parts. */
  use(plugin: PluginParts): () => void;
  onAfter(hook: AsyncHook): () => void;
  on(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  /** Subscribe to the first matching command only; auto-unsubscribes after it fires. */
  once(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  offAll(pattern?: string): void;
  /**
   * Request/response: a responder answers, receiving the command the plugins saw. Identical
   * in-flight requests (same action, target and payload) share one responder run, and each
   * caller keeps its own timeout (default 5000 ms) and `signal`: its abort settles its own
   * promise at once. The responder's cmd.signal aborts, with the caller's reason, once every
   * caller holding the request has aborted. Without a responder this is a dispatch.
   * tests/request-join.test.ts.
   */
  request<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, target: TargetOf<M, A>, payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>, options?: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>>;
  respond(action: string, handler: (cmd: Command) => any | Promise<any>): () => void;
  /** Returns true if a handler is registered for the given action. */
  hasHandler(action: string): boolean;
  /** Returns all registered action names. */
  registeredActions(): string[];
  /**
   * @internal Used by the undo ledger to retrieve an undo handler registered alongside
   * a command handler. Do not call this from application code.
   */
  getUndoHandler(action: string): Handler | undefined;
  /** @internal The `canUndo` registered with an action's undo, for undo history. */
  getUndoCheck(action: string): ((cmd: Command) => boolean) | undefined;
  /** Remove all handlers, plugins, hooks, and listeners. Useful for testing and HMR. */
  clear(): void;
  /** Freeze configuration - rejects register/use/clear after sealing. */
  seal(): void;
  /** Returns true if the bus is sealed. */
  isSealed(): boolean;
  /**
   * Teardown - runs each plugin's dispose(), clears state and settles
   * pending request()s as core:aborted:dispatch. There is no disposed state: the bus stays usable.
   */
  dispose(): void;
}
```

### BaseBus

**Interface** - [src/command-bus.ts:598](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L598)

```ts
export interface BaseBus {
  dispatch(action: string, target: any, payload?: any, options?: DispatchOptions): any;
  /** Read-only dispatch - runs the rules, the steps and the handler, fires afterHooks. No mutation intent. */
  query(action: string, target: any, payload?: any): any;
  /** Fire a domain event - notifies on() listeners, no handler required, no result returned. */
  emit(event: string, data?: any): void;
  register(action: string, handler: any, options?: RegisterOptions): () => void;
  use(plugin: PluginParts): () => void;
  onAfter(hook: any): () => void;
  on(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  once(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  /** Remove all `on()` listeners matching the given pattern, or all listeners if omitted. */
  offAll(pattern?: string): void;
  hasHandler(action: string): boolean;
  /** Returns all registered action names. Useful for introspection and DevTools. */
  registeredActions(): string[];
  clear(): void;
  /**
   * Full teardown - calls clear() and cancels all pending timers/requests. Use in SSR or component-scoped buses.
   * A request() still waiting on its responder settles at once as
   * core:aborted:dispatch with its timer cleared; the responder is not told (only the caller's own signal
   * reaches cmd.signal, on the async bus). There is no disposed state - the bus stays usable - and
   * dispose() works on a sealed bus, which stays sealed. It also runs each installed plugin's
   * `dispose()` first (retry owns timers), before the plugins are dropped.
   */
  dispose(): void;
  /**
   * Seal the bus - prevents further register(), use(), onAfter(), respond() calls.
   * Dispatch, query, emit, on(), once() still work - seal protects the handler/plugin topology,
   * not the observation layer. Listeners via on()/once() can still subscribe after seal.
   * Call after app initialization to lock down the graph in production. Throws BusError
   * with code 'core:refused:bus' on any mutation attempt. clear() is a mutation too and throws
   * on a sealed bus, since it would delete the undo handlers and plugins the seal commits: for
   * HMR, call unsealBus() first, then clear(). dispose() works on a sealed bus and leaves it
   * sealed.
   */
  seal(): void;
  /** Returns true if the bus has been sealed. */
  isSealed(): boolean;
}
```

Structural base interface for both sync and async buses.
Use this as the parameter type in utilities (createChamber, createWorkflow, etc.)
to avoid `as any` casts when working with either bus variant.

### CommandBus

**Interface** - [src/command-bus.ts:639](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L639)

```ts
export interface CommandBus<M extends CommandMap = CommandMap> extends BaseBus {
  /**
   * Sync dispatch. The optional `options.signal` is accepted for type
   * compatibility with `AsyncCommandBus` but **ignored at runtime** - sync
   * dispatches are atomic and not cancelable. Pass a signal here only if
   * you also use the async bus and want a uniform call site.
   */
  dispatch<A extends keyof M & string>(
    action: A,
    target: TargetOf<M, A>,
    payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>,
    options?: DispatchOptions,
  ): CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>;
  /** Read-only dispatch - runs the rules, the steps and the handler, fires afterHooks. */
  query<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, target: TargetOf<M, A>, payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>): CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>;
  /** Fire a domain event - notifies on() listeners, no handler required, no result. */
  emit(event: string, data?: any): void;
  dispatchBatch(commands: BatchCommand[], options?: BatchOptions): BatchResult;
  register<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, handler: (cmd: Command<A, TargetOf<M, A>, PayloadOf<M, A>>) => ResultOf<M, A>, options?: RegisterOptions): () => void;
  use(plugin: PluginParts): () => void;
  onAfter(hook: Hook): () => void;
  on(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  /** Subscribe to the first matching command only; auto-unsubscribes after it fires. */
  once(pattern: string, listener: Listener, options?: ListenerOptions): () => void;
  offAll(pattern?: string): void;
  /**
   * Request/response: a responder answers, a timeout (default 5000 ms) bounds the wait, and
   * `signal` settles the request - before the responder runs if already aborted, at once if
   * aborted while waiting. The sync command carries no signal (see Command.signal), so the
   * responder is not told; without a responder this is a dispatch.
   */
  request<A extends keyof M & string>(action: A, target: TargetOf<M, A>, payload?: PayloadOf<M, A>, options?: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<CommandResult<ResultOf<M, A>>>;
  respond(action: string, handler: (cmd: Command) => any | Promise<any>): () => void;
  /** Returns true if a handler is registered for the given action. */
  hasHandler(action: string): boolean;
  /** Returns all registered action names. */
  registeredActions(): string[];
  /**
   * @internal Used by the undo ledger to retrieve an undo handler registered alongside
   * a command handler. Do not call this from application code.
   */
  getUndoHandler(action: string): Handler | undefined;
  /** @internal The `canUndo` registered with an action's undo, for undo history. */
  getUndoCheck(action: string): ((cmd: Command) => boolean) | undefined;
  /** Remove all handlers, plugins, hooks, and listeners. Useful for testing and HMR. */
  clear(): void;
  /** Freeze configuration - rejects register/use/clear after sealing. */
  seal(): void;
  /** Returns true if the bus is sealed. */
  isSealed(): boolean;
  /**
   * Teardown - runs each plugin's dispose(), clears state and settles
   * pending request()s as core:aborted:dispatch. There is no disposed state: the bus stays usable.
   */
  dispose(): void;
}
```

### CommandPool

**Interface** - [src/command-bus.ts:1509](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L1509)

```ts
export interface CommandPool {
  /** Acquire a command object from the pool. Reuses slots in a circular fashion. */
  acquire(action: string, target: any, payload?: any): Command;
  /** Current pool statistics. */
  stats(): { size: number; acquired: number; cursor: number };
  /** Reset the pool - clears all slots and resets cursor. */
  reset(): void;
  /** Pool capacity. */
  readonly size: number;
}
```

CommandPool - pre-allocates Command objects in a circular buffer to
eliminate garbage collection pauses during dispatch bursts. When the
pool is exhausted, it wraps around and reuses the oldest slot.

**Important**: The pool is a standalone utility - `bus.dispatch()` still
creates its own Command internally and stamps `meta` (ts, id, correlationId).
Pooled commands do NOT have `meta` set. Use `pool.acquire()` for the action/target/payload,
then pass those values to `bus.dispatch(cmd.action, cmd.target, cmd.payload)`.
The bus will create its own internal command with proper metadata.

```ts
const pool = createCommandPool();
const cmd = pool.acquire('cartAdd', cart, { id: 1 });
bus.dispatch(cmd.action, cmd.target, cmd.payload); // bus stamps its own meta

pool.stats(); // { size: 64, acquired: 1, cursor: 1 }
pool.reset(); // Reset cursor and clear all slots
```

### GlobalCommands

**Interface** - [src/chamber.ts:648](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/chamber.ts#L648)

```ts
export interface GlobalCommands {}
```

GlobalCommands - module-augmentation hook that types the SHARED bus
(pinia-style). Augment it once in your app and every `useCommand()` /
`getCommandBus()` call site gets typed dispatch/register with autocomplete
and compile errors:

```ts
declare module 'vapor-chamber' {
  interface GlobalCommands {
    cartAdd: { target: Product; payload: { qty: number }; result: Cart };
    cartClear: { target: null; result: Cart };
  }
}

Unaugmented, everything stays exactly as loose as before (string actions,
`any` targets). Schema users: derive the entries with `InferMap<S>` from
'./schema' instead of writing them by hand.
```

A cell: `value`. An interface, so an entry that wires a reactive backing
extends it with its cell's type: `vapor-chamber/vapor` wires `shallowRef` at
import and declares `Signal<T>` a Vue `ShallowRef<T>`, so a template
unwraps it. A named interface stays `Signal<T>` in every emitted
declaration, so a consumer without that entry never reads `vue`.
Types only. tests/vapor-signal-types.test-d.ts.

```ts
export interface TestBus extends CommandBus<any> {
  /** All dispatched commands in order */
  readonly recorded: RecordedDispatch[];
  /** True if any command with this action was dispatched */
  wasDispatched(action: string): boolean;
  /** All recorded dispatches for a given action */
  getDispatched(action: string): RecordedDispatch[];
  /** Clear the recorded list and listeners */
  clear(): void;
  /** Read-only dispatch - runs the rules, the steps and the handler, fires afterHooks. */
  query(action: string, target: any, payload?: any): CommandResult;
  /** Fire a domain event - notifies on() listeners, no handler required, no result. */
  emit(event: string, data?: any): void;
  /** As the async bus: `null` declares the options of an action a transport sends. */
  register<A extends string>(action: A, handler: ((cmd: Command<A, any, any>) => any) | null, options?: RegisterOptions): () => void;
  /** Returns all registered action names. */
  registeredActions(): string[];
  /**

   * Safe to compare with `toEqual` in any test framework.
   */
  snapshot(): RecordedDispatch[];
  /**

   * through `index` (inclusive). Useful for asserting the sequence of events
   * that led to a particular state.

  travelTo(index: number): Command[];

   * the last occurrence of `action`. Useful for "what happened before this action".

  travelToAction(action: string): Command[];

  inspect(): BusInspection;
```

### ActionScope

A plugin's action filter, the `actions` option of every plugin that takes
one and the `actions` it declares to the bus: absent or `[]` is every action
(ActionScope's own rule, stated here once), each entry an action name or a pattern
(`'cart*'`, `'*'`). Read by the bus alone. Log s35.146 and s35.148,

### AnnounceOptions

**Type alias** - [src/a11y.ts:19](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/a11y.ts#L19)

```ts
export type AnnounceOptions = {
  /** Interrupt what is being read (a failure); default polite (a success, a page change). */
  assertive?: boolean;
};
```

vapor-chamber - status messages for assistive technology.

`announce(message)` says something to a screen reader without moving focus
(WCAG 4.1.3, status messages): a failed command, a saved form, a page that
changed. Every feature that needs it goes through here, so a document has
ONE pair of live regions (polite, assertive), created on first use, instead
of one per feature. That is the pattern of Angular CDK's LiveAnnouncer and
React Aria's announce(), and the reason a region is not the router's or the
directive's own.

The library holds no words: what is announced is data (a failure's message,
a backend problem's `detail`, already localized; a page's
title). An app that wants its own words or its own status bar takes the
announcing over with `setAnnouncer(fn)`, and `setAnnouncer(null)` hands it
back. A no-op outside a browser. tests/a11y-announce.test.ts.

```ts
export type BatchOptions = {
  continueOnError?: boolean;
  /**
   * All-or-nothing semantics: if any command fails, automatically run the
   * registered undo handler for every command that already succeeded (in reverse order).
   * Requires undo handlers to be registered via `register(action, handler, { undo })`.
   * Commands without an undo handler are skipped during rollback.
   * Mutually exclusive with `continueOnError`.
   */
  transactional?: boolean;
  /**
   * AbortSignal applied to the whole batch. Aborting before the batch starts
   * skips it entirely; aborting mid-flight stops further commands from
   * dispatching (the in-flight one runs to completion since per-command
   * abort already happened or is the handler's responsibility) and the
   * batch result is
   * `{ ok: false, error: BusError('core:aborted:dispatch'), results: [...partial] }`
   * - a BusError rather than the raw DOMException so the code is queryable
   * (see `abortedResult`; a caller-supplied `signal.reason` is passed through
   * unchanged). Under `transactional`, rollback runs first and
   * `successCount` is reported as 0.
   * Async bus only - sync `dispatchBatch` accepts the option for type
   * uniformity but ignores it.
   */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
};
```

```ts
   * sets it: async handlers may listen to `cmd.signal.aborted` /
   * `cmd.signal.addEventListener('abort', ...)` to short-circuit work, and
   * transports (HTTP) forward it to the underlying fetch. A sync dispatch
   * ignores its own `{ signal }` option: it is atomic. On either bus a step's
   * ticket (`PluginParts.begin`) may set it, combined with any already there,
   * so work a handler starts and does not await can be cancelled by the step
   * that owns the signal (tests/work-steps.test.ts).
   */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
};
```

```ts
export type CommandMeta = {
  /**
   * Wall-clock stamp for correlation and audit - NOT a timing instrument.
   *
   * Read from `Date.now()` **once per microtask turn** and shared by every
   * command dispatched inside that turn. The first command of each turn carries
   * an exact stamp; the 2nd..nth of the same synchronous run repeat it. Since
   * `Date.now()` is millisecond-resolution and a typical burst is
   * sub-millisecond, those commands would almost always have received the same
   * number anyway - what is actually given up is intra-burst resolution in
   * bursts long enough to cross a millisecond (a thousand-command burst reads
   * as instantaneous). Bought ~15-25ns per dispatch; measured in
   * `tests/clock-source-ab.test.ts` (v1.6.0, 2026-08-24).
   *
   * **Ordering does not depend on this field.** `meta.id` is a monotonic
   * counter and stays unique and ordered - use it, not `ts`, to sequence
   * commands.
   *
   * **Do not measure durations with it, cached or not.** `Date.now()` is wall
   * clock: millisecond-resolution and *not monotonic*, so an NTP correction or
   * a clock change can move it, backwards included. That was true before this
   * cache and is not a consequence of it. For real timing use
   * `performance.now()` in a plugin; on a hot loop use `createFastLane()`,
   * which stamps no meta at all.
   */

  /**
   * Unique, monotonically increasing command ID - the ordering key.
   *

   * counter (`configureUid` swaps it; `crypto.randomUUID` is the documented
   * opt-in for cross-process auditing, not the default).
   */
  id: string;
  /** ID of the command that caused this one (set manually via payload.__causationId). */
  causationId?: string;
  /** Correlation ID for tracing a chain of commands (propagates from parent). */
  correlationId?: string;
  /**

   * `Idempotency-Key` header, or that name in a batched command's or a
   * frame's `headers`, so the backend can reject duplicate writes.

   * the retry (an action declared idempotent) stamps it. Never the command's
   * content: an app's own key as given, an outbox record's key, else this
   * dispatch's `id` (tests/idempotency-key.test.ts).
   */
  idempotencyKey?: string;
  /**
   * The 2xx response a transport's reply arrived in, Fetch's members (a 202
   * says accepted, not finished: RFC 9110 15.3.3). Always present, `undefined`
   * for a local handler; a non-2xx answer is the error's.

   * endpoints) stamp it post-hoc via plugins so downstream plugins, hooks, and

   * commands (e.g. skip re-broadcasting a `'sync'` command, or audit-log

   * an undo handler and `'redo'` on a redo and what its handler dispatches

   * neither, nor a `'sync'` command (a change an app's sync layer mirrored from
```

### CommandResult

**Type alias** - [src/command-bus.ts:206](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L206)

```ts
export type CommandResult<V = any> =
  | { ok: true; value?: V; error?: undefined }
  | { ok: false; error: Error; value?: undefined };
```

Result of a dispatch/query - a discriminated union on `ok`.

`if (result.ok)` narrows away `error`; on the failure arm `error` is a
guaranteed `Error` (no `!` or `?.` needed). `value` stays optional on the
success arm because void commands legitimately produce no value.

### CommandState

**Type alias** - [src/command-state.ts:86](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-state.ts#L86)

```ts
export type CommandState = {
  /**
   * In flight for this key, bus-wide: any dispatch counts, from any caller.
   * Keyed like `commandKey`, so object targets match by value. `pending(action)`
   * is the exact key `(action, undefined)`, not "any target of this action".
   * Its own signal, written only when its count crosses 0 <-> 1. Counting
   * starts at the first `pending()` call or `anyPending` read: a dispatch
   * already in flight then is not counted.
   */
  pending(action: string, target?: unknown): Readonly<Signal<boolean>>;
  /** Any command in flight on the bus, written on 0 <-> 1. Reading it starts counting. */
  readonly anyPending: Readonly<Signal<boolean>>;
  /** The bus's recent failures, newest last, at most `maxSize`. */
  readonly errors: Readonly<Signal<readonly Error[]>>;
  /** The bus's most recent failure. */
  readonly lastError: Readonly<Signal<Error | null>>;
  /** Wipe `errors` and `lastError`. Pending keys are untouched. */
  clear(): void;
  /** Call `fn` after a fact moved a value this state holds. Returns the unsubscribe. */
  subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void;
  /** Release this handle, once. The last one releases the state. */
  dispose(): void;
};
```

One handle on a bus's command state (`commandState`).

### DeadLetterMode

**Type alias** - [src/command-bus.ts:372](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/command-bus.ts#L372)

```ts
export type DeadLetterMode = 'error' | 'throw' | 'ignore' | ((cmd: Command) => CommandResult);
```

Dead letter mode - what to do when a command has no registered handler.
- `'error'` (default): returns `{ ok: false, error }`
- `'throw'`: throws the error
- `'ignore'`: returns `{ ok: true, value: undefined }`
- function: called with the command, return value used as result

To make a dispatch wait for a handler that registers later, give the bus a
`buffer` (`createBuffer`): it takes precedence for a dispatch, and a query
still answers by this mode.

```ts
  /** Reactive set of fields the user has interacted with. */

  /** True when no validation errors exist. */
  readonly isValid: { readonly value: boolean };

  /** True while async validation is running. */
  isValidating: Signal<boolean>;
  /** True when either validating or submitting - use for disabling submit buttons. */
  isBusy: Signal<boolean>;
  /** Set a single field value and re-run validation. */

  /** Mark a field as touched (shows errors for that field). */

  /** Validate and call onSubmit. Returns true on success; false on validation failure, a reset during validation, or a submit already in flight. */
  submit(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Reset all fields to their initial values and clear errors/touched state. */
  reset(): void;

   * `aria-describedby`: the spread's value overrides the attribute.

  /** The id for the element holding a field's message: stable, unique per form, a valid id. */
  errorId<K extends keyof T>(field: K): string;
  /** The first field, in declaration order, whose error is shown - the one to focus after a failed submit. */
  firstInvalid(): keyof T | undefined;
  /** Attach a plugin to the form's internal command bus. */
  use(plugin: PluginParts): void;
  /** The underlying command bus - for advanced use (DevTools, testing). */
  bus: CommandBus;
  /**
```

```ts
   * string) takes that default; anything above

   * a negative value times out immediately.

   * 503) for any method; an uncertain one, or an answer with a declared wait,
   * only for an idempotent method or an `Idempotency-Key`. `maxAttempts` is
   * the bus's bound (`RetryOptions`): attempts in total, the first included,
   * default 3. `false` sends once. Default: **on for a GET through a client,
   * off for any other method and through `postCommand`**; `{}` turns it on.

   * no reply, a 502 or a 504 is not re-sent and fails with
   * `context.outcome: 'unknown'`. A re-send waits the declared wait, else the
   * async bus's schedule: random under 200 ms x 2^n, capped at 20 s
   * (docs/retry.md). tests/one-client.test.ts.

  signal?: AbortSignal;

   * will then only re-read the token from the DOM on retry).

  /** Additional headers merged into every request. A name matches in any case: its first spelling is kept and the last value wins (the Fetch Standard's "set"), so it goes out once. */

  /** Called when a 401 session-expired response is received */
  onSessionExpired?: (status: number) => void;
  /**
   * Stamps `context.silent` on a thrown error so a caller-provided global error
   * handler can skip it - for fire-and-forget requests (best-effort
   * telemetry, background prefetch) that shouldn't surface UI noise.
   * Default: false.
   */
  silent?: boolean;
  /**
   * Resolve a 304 Not Modified instead of throwing it. A 304 answers a
   * conditional request the app sent itself (`If-None-Match`,
   * `If-Modified-Since`): "what you hold is current", not a failure. Opted
   * in, the response resolves as it is (`status` 304, `ok` false as Fetch
   * says, `data` the empty body); off, it throws its `remote:` failure like
   * any non-2xx. Never cached. Default: false.
   * tests/http-not-modified.test.ts.
   */
  resolveNotModified?: boolean;
};
```

vapor-chamber - HTTP client

Written to the CDCC guideline of small, single-purpose functions
(docs/whitepaper.md 3.5). It is a guideline: no lint rule checks it.

What it does beyond a bare `fetch`:
 - `AbortSignal.any` with manual fallback for older environments
 - The async bus's retry schedule (full jitter, docs/retry.md) for a re-send it decides itself
 - A declared wait sets when to re-send, never whether: `Retry-After` (RFC 9110), else `RateLimit` `t`, else `X-RateLimit-Reset`
 - 419 CSRF refresh coalesces concurrent requests (no duplicate refreshes)
 - `session-expired` CustomEvent + configurable callback
 - The caller's abort (`transport:aborted:request`) distinct from no reply in time (`transport:timeout:reply`)

### HttpRequestConfig

**Type alias** - [src/http.ts:851](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/http.ts#L851)

```ts
export type HttpRequestConfig = HttpConfig & {
  /** HTTP method. Default: 'GET' */
  method?: HttpMethod;
  /** Request body (auto-serialized if object, passthrough for FormData) */
  data?: unknown;
  /** Query parameters - supports arrays and nested objects */
  params?: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** Base URL prepended to relative paths */
  baseURL?: string;
  /** Response parsing mode. Default: 'json' */
  responseType?: ResponseType;
  /**
   * Enable LRU caching for GET. `true` = default TTL, no stale window.
   * `{ ttl }` sets the fresh-window duration. `{ staleTtl }` opts into
   * stale-while-revalidate: a hit within `ttl + staleTtl` past `ttl` is
   * served instantly with `{ stale: true, revalidation: Promise }` attached,
   * while a background fetch refreshes the entry. `serveStaleOnError` is a
   * separate opt-in: a transient failure (timeout/network/5xx) with ANY
   * retained entry (even past its stale window) resolves to
   * `{ stale: true, servedOnError: true, error }` instead of rejecting.
   */
  cache?: boolean | { ttl?: number; staleTtl?: number; serveStaleOnError?: boolean };
  /**
   * Enable request deduplication for GET. Default: true. A concurrent GET
   * of the same URL joins the one in flight and shares its outcome, but
   * keeps its own `signal`: aborting it rejects that caller's promise only.
   * The fetch is cancelled once every caller holding it has aborted; a
   * caller without a signal holds it until it lands.
   * (`tests/http-dedupe-signal.test.ts`) A `silent` read and one without
   * `silent` are two requests, even at the same moment: joined, they would
   * share one failure, and one caller's `silent` mark would reach the other
   * (`tests/silent-dedupe.test.ts`).
   */
  dedupe?: boolean;
  /**
   * Fetch's cache mode for this request (`RequestInit.cache`), for the
   * browser's cache and the client's own store (`cache`) alike. `'no-cache'`
   * asks the server before a stored copy is used, sending its `ETag`: a router
   * refresh reads so. `'reload'` reads past a stored copy and stores the
   * answer. `'no-store'` neither reads nor stores. Absent: Fetch's default. A
   * read in one mode never joins a read in another.
   * tests/http-cache-mode.test.ts, tests/cache-groups.test.ts.
   */
  cacheMode?: RequestCache;
  /** @internal marks a CSRF-retried request */
  _csrfRetried?: boolean;
};
```

**Type alias** - [src/http.ts:86](https://github.com/lucianofedericopereira/vapor-chamber/blob/main/src/http.ts#L86)

```ts
export type HttpResponse<T = unknown> = {
  data: T;
  status: number;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  ok: boolean;

   * The final URL, after any redirect Fetch followed (Fetch's `Response.url`).
   * Always set by `createHttpClient` and `postCommand`; optional for an app's
   * own client.
   */
  url?: string;
  /** True when Fetch followed a redirect to reach `url` (`Response.redirected`). */
  redirected?: boolean;
  /** True when this response was served from a stale (past-fresh) cache entry. */
  stale?: boolean;
  /** Present on a stale hit: resolves with the fresh response once the background revalidation lands. */
  revalidation?: Promise<HttpResponse<T>>;
  /** True when this is a retained cache entry served in place of a transient failure (`cache.serveStaleOnError`). */
  servedOnError?: boolean;
  /** The transient error `servedOnError` masked - surfaced alongside the stale data, never silently dropped. */
  error?: unknown;
};
```
